title: When the Will Sings
premise: Emrys Eastwick, coroner of the fog-bound town of Hollowmere, receives two letters the same morning: one confessing to a drowning ruled accidental fifteen years ago, the other promising a second death unless the case stays closed. As the statute of limitations ticks down, Emrys discovers the drowned man was his own estranged brother, and the confession's handwriting belongs to someone he loves. The killer is Marlow, the found-family friend who took Emrys in after the drowning—acting to protect Emrys from a brother who returned to blackmail him. In the end, Emrys must choose between the law he serves and the family he built, testifying to the truth and losing Hollowmere's trust, but gaining an honest, fragile new beginning with the one person who told him the truth before the deadline.
about_author: Petra Amberdale is the pen name of a former rural registrar who spent a decade recording births and deaths in a coastal village, where every file seemed to hide a second story. She now writes mysteries from a drafty cottage, aided by an opinionated cat and a weakness for unsolved local legends.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Morning
chapters.summary: Emrys Eastwick's POV. On an ordinary Monday, two letters arrive: a detailed confession to a fifteen-year-old drowning, and an unsigned threat promising 'a second verse.' Emrys, who prides himself on knowing every grave in Hollowmere, feels the ground shift. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Grave That Has No Name
chapters.summary: Emrys reopens the file on the drowning victim: a John Doe never claimed, buried in plot forty-one. The confession names the spot with unsettling precision. His deputy, Sable, urges him to let sleeping water lie. Emotional beat: the first crack in Emrys's ordered world.

chapters.title: Ink and Intent
chapters.summary: Emrys compares the confession's handwriting to records in his office and finds an impossible match: the penmanship resembles letters he's received for years from his benefactor, Marlow Quinn, who took him in as a grieving teenager. Emotional beat: betrayal's first cold touch.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Sundays
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Emrys's POV. The aftermath of the drowning: a boy with no family, taken in by Marlow, the kindly innkeeper who fed the whole town. The chapter builds the found-family warmth that everything now threatens. Emotional beat: love as shelter.

chapters.title: The Statute's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Emrys learns the prosecution window closes in thirty days. The second letter escalates: 'Close it, or the innkeeper sings a duet.' He realizes the blackmailer knows Marlow. Emotional beat: a clock begins to tick.

chapters.title: Sable's Skepticism
chapters.summary: Sable Okafor's POV. The deputy suspects Emrys is chasing ghosts and files a quiet report to the county. Sable's loyalty wars with procedure. Emotional beat: friendship under strain.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Emrys exhumes plot forty-one with a court order. The bones tell a different story: a healed fracture, a ring fused to a finger. The ring's engraving—a family crest Emrys recognizes from his own childhood. Emotional beat: the dead man has a name, and it's his own surname.

chapters.title: Eastwick
chapters.summary: Emrys confronts the town archive: the John Doe was Tomas Eastwick, the brother who abandoned him, presumed gone abroad. The confession's 'accidental drowning' now reads as something else entirely. Emotional beat: grief reopened, identity destabilized.

chapters.title: The Inn at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Emrys watches Marlow at the inn, cataloguing small lies: a locked room, a burn-scarred ledger, a boat engine replaced the spring after the drowning. Marlow catches him looking and smiles. Emotional beat: suspicion poisoning gratitude.

chapters.title: A Second Letter, A First Lie
chapters.summary: The blackmailer's third letter arrives with a photograph of Marlow on the dock the night Tomas died. Emrys realizes the blackmailer was there too—and is circling closer. Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Introduce Wren Halloway, a young archivist and runaway who has informally become Emrys's family, helping sort the cold-case files. Wren finds a missing page from the original coroner's report—Emrys's predecessor's report was altered. Emotional beat: found family deepens even as old family rots.

chapters.title: The Altered Report
chapters.summary: Emrys traces the forgery: his predecessor was paid to rule the drowning accidental. The payer's signature matches Marlow's early business accounts. Emotional beat: the case was closed by purchase, not by truth.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Tide Line
chapters.summary: Emrys confronts Marlow on the beach. Marlow admits he was there that night: Tomas returned to extort him, they struggled, Tomas fell. Marlow insists it was an accident he then buried to protect the town—and Emrys. Emotional beat: love and duty collide.

chapters.title: The Blackmail Unmasked
chapters.summary: Emrys sets a trap using the inn's mail. The blackmailer is revealed as Deputy Sable's estranged father, a former dockworker who witnessed the struggle and has bled Marlow quietly for years. Emotional beat: the threat has a face, but the moral tangle tightens.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Days
chapters.summary: With the statute expiring, the county prosecutor demands Emrys either charge someone or close the case permanently. Sable, humiliated by her father, offers Emrys her testimony. Emotional beat: allies realign around painful truths.

chapters.title: What Marlow Built
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren uncovers how Marlow's charity propped up half of Hollowmere—jobs, debts forgiven, the school roof. Convicting him could break the town that raised Emrys. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made concrete.

chapters.title: The Confession, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Emrys reads Marlow's original letter to him in the inn's empty kitchen. Marlow explains why he confessed now: he is dying, and wanted Emrys to hear it from him, not a courtroom. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: The Storm
chapters.summary: Climax begins. The blackmailer, facing exposure, breaks into the inn to destroy the ledger and force a final payment. Marlow confronts him; Emrys arrives mid-struggle on the dock in a rising storm. Emotional beat: everything converges on the water.

chapters.title: Second Verse
chapters.summary: Climax. On the same dock where Tomas died, the blackmailer attacks Emrys; Marlow takes the blow meant for him. Sable and Wren arrive; the blackmailer is arrested for assault and extortion. Marlow, gravely injured, whispers for Emrys to 'finish it honestly.' Emotional beat: sacrifice and clarity.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Emrys testifies to the full truth: the accidental struggle, the covered-up death, the bought report. Marlow, recovering, pleads guilty to obstruction. The statute expires mid-hearing, but Emrys testifies anyway—duty fulfilled not by deadline, but by choice. Emotional beat: integrity at last.

chapters.title: Plot Forty-One, Renamed
chapters.summary: The town buries Tomas Eastwick under his own name, with Emrys speaking the eulogy. Some neighbors turn away from Marlow's inn; others bring casseroles to the recovering old man. Wren moves into the room above the office. Emotional beat: mourning, forgiveness, family redefined.

chapters.title: When the Will Sings
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Emrys's POV. A year later, Emrys walks the cemetery naming every grave, ending at plot forty-one. Marlow serves community service tending the grounds; Sable and Emrys share Sunday dinners. A new letter arrives—ordinary, from a grieving widow—and Emrys opens it without fear. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
